title: Variable
code:
const {{name}} = "{{value}}";
console.log({{name}});
description: Store a value with a descriptive name.
explanation: Store a value with a descriptive name.
usage: Use this when you need to store a value with a descriptive name.
mistakes: const prevents reassignment, but does not freeze object contents.

title: Numbers
code:
const total = 12.5 * 3;
console.log(total);
description: Calculate with numbers.
explanation: Calculate with numbers.
usage: Use this when you need to calculate with numbers.
mistakes: Floating-point math may need rounding for display; do not use binary floats for exact cents.

title: Template string
code:
const name = "Alex";
console.log(`Hello, ${name}!`);
description: Insert a value into a string.
explanation: Insert a value into a string.
usage: Use this when you need to insert a value into a string.
mistakes: Interpolation uses backticks, not ordinary quotes.

title: Condition
code:
const score = 82;
if (score >= 60) { console.log("Passed"); } else { console.log("Try again"); }
description: Choose behavior based on a condition.
explanation: Choose behavior based on a condition.
usage: Use this when you need to choose behavior based on a condition.
mistakes: Use === for equality and avoid assigning inside a condition.

title: For loop
code: for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) { console.log(i); }
description: Repeat an action a fixed number of times.
explanation: Repeat an action a fixed number of times.
usage: Use this when you need to repeat an action a fixed number of times.
mistakes: The loop ends before the upper bound; arrays are zero indexed.

title: Array
code:
const items = ["HTML", "CSS", "JavaScript"];
console.log(items[0]);
description: Store an ordered collection.
explanation: Store an ordered collection.
usage: Use this when you need to store an ordered collection.
mistakes: Reading a missing array index gives undefined.

title: Object
code:
const student = { name: "Alex", score: 92 };
console.log(student.name);
description: Group related named values.
explanation: Group related named values.
usage: Use this when you need to group related named values.
mistakes: Property names are case sensitive.

title: Function
description: Create a reusable calculation.
explanation: Create a reusable calculation.
usage: Use this when you need to create a reusable calculation.
mistakes: Return a result instead of only logging it if callers need the value.

title: Array map
code:
const doubled = [1, 2, 3].map(number => number * 2);
console.log(doubled);
description: Transform each item into a new value.
explanation: Transform each item into a new value.
usage: Use this when you need to transform each item into a new value.
mistakes: map returns a new array; keep its callback free of unintended mutations.

title: Array filter
code:
const passing = [45, 82, 91].filter(score => score >= 60);
console.log(passing);
description: Keep items that meet a condition.
explanation: Keep items that meet a condition.
usage: Use this when you need to keep items that meet a condition.
mistakes: filter keeps items only when the callback is truthy.

title: Find item
code:
const student = [{ id: 1, name: "Alex" }].find(item => item.id === 1);
console.log(student?.name ?? "Not found");
description: Find one item and handle a missing result.
explanation: Find one item and handle a missing result.
usage: Use this when you need to find one item and handle a missing result.
mistakes: find may return undefined; optional chaining handles that case.

title: For of
code: for (const item of ["HTML", "CSS"]) { console.log(item); }
description: Iterate directly over collection values.
explanation: Iterate directly over collection values.
usage: Use this when you need to iterate directly over collection values.
mistakes: Use for...of for values; for...in iterates property keys.

title: DOM text
code:
const heading = document.querySelector("h1");
if (heading) heading.textContent = "Hello from JavaScript";
description: Update a heading on a web page.
explanation: Update a heading on a web page.
usage: Use this when you need to update a heading on a web page.
mistakes: querySelector may return null and requires a browser document.

title: Click event
code:
const button = document.querySelector("button");
button?.addEventListener("click", () => { button.textContent = "Clicked!"; });
description: Respond to a button click.
explanation: Respond to a button click.
usage: Use this when you need to respond to a button click.
mistakes: Wait until the button exists before registering the listener.

title: Create element
description: Add text to a page without interpreting HTML.
explanation: Add text to a page without interpreting HTML.
usage: Use this when you need to add text to a page without interpreting HTML.
mistakes: Prefer textContent for user text rather than innerHTML.

title: JSON parse
code:
const json = '{"name":"Alex"}';
try { console.log(JSON.parse(json)); } catch (error) { console.error("Invalid JSON", error); }
description: Read JSON while handling malformed input.
explanation: Read JSON while handling malformed input.
usage: Use this when you need to read JSON while handling malformed input.
mistakes: JSON uses double-quoted keys and strings; malformed text throws.

title: JSON stringify
code:
const data = { language: "JavaScript", useful: true };
console.log(JSON.stringify(data, null, 2));
description: Convert an object to formatted JSON.
explanation: Convert an object to formatted JSON.
usage: Use this when you need to convert an object to formatted JSON.
mistakes: Undefined values and functions do not serialize like normal data.

title: Async fetch
description: Request JSON and handle HTTP errors.
explanation: Request JSON and handle HTTP errors.
usage: Use this when you need to request JSON and handle HTTP errors.
mistakes: fetch does not reject for HTTP 404; check response.ok.

title: Promise
code:
const wait = ms => new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, ms));
wait(100).then(() => console.log("Ready"));
description: Represent a value that arrives later.
explanation: Represent a value that arrives later.
usage: Use this when you need to represent a value that arrives later.
mistakes: A promise is asynchronous; use then or await to read its result.

title: Error handling
description: Catch and report an error.
explanation: Catch and report an error.
usage: Use this when you need to catch and report an error.
mistakes: Catch only errors you can handle or report clearly.

title: Destructuring
code:
const { name, score = 0 } = { name: "Alex" };
console.log(name, score);
description: Extract object fields with defaults.
explanation: Extract object fields with defaults.
usage: Use this when you need to extract object fields with defaults.
mistakes: A default applies to undefined, not null.

title: Spread
description: Create an array without mutating the original.
explanation: Create an array without mutating the original.
usage: Use this when you need to create an array without mutating the original.
mistakes: Spread only copies one level; nested objects still share references.

title: Reduce
code:
const total = [10, 20, 30].reduce((sum, value) => sum + value, 0);
console.log(total);
description: Combine array values into a single result.
explanation: Combine array values into a single result.
usage: Use this when you need to combine array values into a single result.
mistakes: An initial accumulator handles empty arrays safely.

title: Map collection
description: Store key-value pairs in a Map.
explanation: Store key-value pairs in a Map.
usage: Use this when you need to store key-value pairs in a Map.
mistakes: Map keys are not object properties; use get and set.

title: Set uniqueness
code:
const unique = [...new Set([1, 1, 2, 3])];
console.log(unique);
description: Remove duplicate primitive values.
explanation: Remove duplicate primitive values.
usage: Use this when you need to remove duplicate primitive values.
mistakes: Set compares object references, not object contents.

title: Module export
code: export function greet(name) { return `Hello, ${name}!`; }
description: Expose a function from an ES module.
explanation: Expose a function from an ES module.
usage: Use this when you need to expose a function from an ES module.
mistakes: Exports require an ES module; use .mjs in Node or type="module" in HTML.
requirements: Save as .mjs for Node ES modules

title: Complete grade summary
description: Filter a class list and print passing students.
explanation: Filter a class list and print passing students.
usage: Use this when you need to filter a class list and print passing students.
mistakes: An empty filtered array is valid; do not assume somebody passed.
